body:
Guatemala organic decaf coffee , a Huehuetenango lot decaffeinated with the Mountain Water Process. Balanced and cocoa-forward with a little apple brightness behind it. Certified organic, water only, no solvents.
Roasted to order in Concord, California and shipped within 72 hours. Available in 6 oz, 12 oz and 24 oz bags.
Guatemala decaf coffee from Huehuetenango is what a lot of people picture when they think of a classic cup of coffee: balanced, a little bright, chocolatey, nothing out of place. Huehuetenango is the highest and driest of Guatemala’s growing regions, up against the Mexican border, and it produces beans with the density to come through decaffeination with their character intact. This lot is certified organic and processed with water only. We roast it to order on our Buckeye roasters in Concord, California.
What Guatemala Decaf Coffee Tastes Like
Cocoa and brown sugar up front, a red apple brightness in the middle, and a clean, medium finish. The body is medium and the whole thing is balanced in a way that makes it easy to drink every day. It is the decaf for someone who does not want fruit bombs or heavy earth, just a well made cup.
The Mountain Water Process, which is what Royal Select means, removes the caffeine using pure water and a filter, with no chemical solvents. On a balanced coffee like this, the method is nearly invisible, which is the point.
Origin and Region: Guatemala, Huehuetenango (HHT)
Certification: Organic
Decaf Process: Mountain Water Process (MWP), Royal Select, water only
Altitude: 1,500 to 1,900 meters
Bean Process: Washed before decaffeination
Cup Notes: Cocoa, brown sugar, red apple
Body: Medium
Acidity: Medium, gentle
Best For: Drip, pour over, French press. Black or with milk
Decaf Is Not Caffeine Free
The honest part first. Roughly 97 percent of the caffeine is removed, which leaves a small residual amount in every cup. A mug of this has about as much caffeine as a few sips of regular coffee. If you have been told to avoid caffeine entirely, talk to your doctor rather than relying on decaf.
The decaffeination happens before the beans reach us. We buy the green coffee already processed, then roast it here. If you want the chemistry, Wikipedia’s overview of decaffeination covers the water and solvent methods in detail. What we control is the roast and the freshness, and those are the two things that separate good decaf from the stale supermarket version that gave decaf its reputation.
Roasted Medium, On Purpose
Decaffeinated beans take heat faster and darken sooner than regular green coffee, so we run this on its own gentler profile. Medium is the right default. It keeps the apple brightness and brings out the cocoa, which is the balance Huehuetenango is known for.
Medium-Dark works if you drink with milk and want more chocolate, less apple. Light is possible but the Costa Rica is a better pick for a bright roast. Our guide to choosing the perfect roast covers the tradeoffs.
Roasted After You Order, Not Pulled Off a Shelf
Nothing here is pre-roasted and warehoused. Your order comes in, we roast it, and it ships within 72 hours with a roast date on the bag. Coffee is at its best roughly 7 to 21 days off the roast, and decaf is no exception. In fact decaf fades faster once roasted, because the porous beans lose aromatics sooner, so freshness matters more here than it does with regular coffee.
We roast about 25,000 pounds a year on two Buckeye roasters at 1717 Solano Way in Concord. Family owned since 2021, FDA registered, open to the public. Visit the roastery in Concord if you are local.
How to Brew Guatemala Decaf Coffee
This is an all-rounder. Drip, pour over and French press all work, and it is one of the few decafs that is good both black and with milk. If you have an automatic drip machine and want one decaf to keep next to it, this is a strong choice.
Start around 1:16, roughly 22 grams of coffee to 350 grams of water.
Order Guatemala decaf coffee whole bean if you can. Decaffeinated beans go stale faster once ground, so grinding at home makes a bigger difference here than with regular coffee. If you order ground, pick the grind for your brewer at checkout. Our perfect brew guide covers every method.
Which Size to Buy
The 6 oz bag of Guatemala decaf coffee is $12 and gives you roughly ten to twelve cups, enough to find out whether this is your evening coffee. The 12 oz bag is $23 and is the size most households land on for decaf kept alongside regular coffee. The 24 oz bag is $43 for people who drink decaf as their main coffee. All three roast on the same schedule, so the larger bag is not older coffee.

Sítio Serra Negra is a small-farm gem from grower Douglas Moreira da Silva — a limited, single-lot microlot built around the Catucaí cultivar and the natural process. The cup is classic Brazil with a lift: brown sugar sweetness, ripe yellow fruit, and a bright citric finish. In short, it is comfort and brightness in the same mug.
About Sítio Serra Negra
The name means “black mountain ridge,” and like all sítios , this is family-scale farming — the kind of small property behind much of Brazil’s most exciting coffee today. For this lot, the cherries were processed as a natural. They dry whole in the sun, and the slow fermentation inside the fruit builds sweetness and fruit character. Naturals demand constant attention, because uneven drying invites defects. Done well, however, the reward is a cup like this one: sweet, expressive, and clean. Catucaí helps too. The cultivar is a Brazilian favorite for productive, resilient trees that still cup beautifully.
What’s in the Cup
Brown sugar arrives first, deep and comforting. Then ripe yellow fruit fills the middle — think ripe stone fruit warmed by the sun. Finally, a citric brightness snaps the finish clean. It is an easy recommendation for anyone who wants to try a natural for the first time. Consequently, this coffee drinks beautifully as a pour-over or drip, and it makes a sweet, lively iced coffee. For filter brewing, start with a 1:16 ratio and adjust to taste.
Like all of our microlots , this is a limited harvest — once this lot is gone, it’s gone. Explore the collection for more small-lot discoveries. Or better yet, let us bring coffees like this to your door with the Brazilian Coffee Lovers Club . Members receive a featured single-farm coffee each month, plus 5% off every microlot. body:
Andrés trained at Tecnicafé in Cauca before joining the renowned Finca El Paraíso, where he led soil studies and process standardization. That technical foundation is shown here with a cup that's fruit-forward and precise in equal measure. Combining these coffees reflects what Andrés set out to build: deliberate craft at the intersection of process and variety. What we get is a complex cup layered with summer’s brightest flavors.
This is a blend of two different offerings produced by Andres Martinez, a semi-washed Gesha, and a honey blackberry co-ferment Caturra.
ORIGIN Cauca, Colombia
VARIETALS Gesha, Caturra
PROCESS Semi-washed, co-ferment
Gesha: Coffee is hand-picked and sorted, where 95% are fully ripe and fermented with added beer yeast for 48 hours. The coffee is depulped and fermented in plastic tanks for 24 hours, with constant mixing to ensure a uniform fermentation process. It is dried in two phases: first at a lower temperature for seven days, then at a higher temperature (below 40°C) until it reaches 12% moisture.
Caturra: Ripe cherries are selected and floated to remove defects, then depulped while keeping the mucilage intact as part of the honey process. Fresh "Castilla blackberries" are blended to prepare the "coffee mosto", which is fermented anaerobically with "enology yeast" for four days to preserve the fruit’s tannic profile. Once the mosto is ready, the coffee beans are added to the tank, allowing both the coffee and the fermented blackberry mosto to co-ferment for an additional four days in a sealed tanks. After this fermentation, the coffee undergoes a light wash to remove any excess of fruit. The coffee is dried on sun-bed driers for 10 to 15 days until it reaches 11% moisture content.
Our flavor notes: Fresh florals, smashed lemons, juicy blackberries
Net Wt. 12oz / 340g

Locally Roasted for Peak Freshness & Flavor
We take pride in roasting our coffee locally to ensure you experience the freshest flavors. By roasting in small batches and directly from the bean to the cup, we preserve the unique characteristics of each batch. This approach guarantees that your coffee is at its peak flavor when it reaches you.
How Costa Rica’s Highlands Shape Our Coffee’s Flavor
Grown in the high altitudes of the Central Highlands, this coffee benefits from the unique climate and soil of the region. The altitude and the rich volcanic soil contribute to the coffee's well-defined acidity and vibrant, bright notes. The careful cultivation and climate conditions of the region are key to developing the delicate flavors that make each cup stand out.

body:
Most coffee shops wouldn't bother with a decaf coffee, let alone a blend to showcase how good it can actually taste. That’s when Uncanny Decaf was born. This blend is intended to bring out the balance and flavor that our speciality blends have while getting decaf to taste like real coffee.
So if you try it and don't believe a decaf can be that good, think again. Take a sip... simply UNCANNY! A decaf coffee that is not the same derivative or bland replacement of caffeinated coffee. Let us all rejoice in the glory decaf.
Mountain Water Decaffeination
Mountain Water processing is a 100% chemical free decaffeination process that uses water and carbon filtration to remove caffeine from coffee. Descamex (Descafeinadores Mexicanos), the company that developed this specific water process, sources the water used in their processing from the glacial waters of Pico de Orizaba, Mexico's highest mountain (hence, mountain water).
Sugar Cane Decaffeination
The Sugar Cane Decaf Process, unique to Colombia, enhances coffee quality by increasing sweetness and preserving complexity. It involves fermenting and distilling sugar cane to obtain ethyl acetate (EA), derived directly from sugarcane. When coffee is introduced, the caffeine is extracted, infusing sweetness. After extraction, steam removes the EA, leaving less than 5ppm in the batch. Ethyl acetate, found in younger wines, imparts fruity aromas and flavors, and a batch of sugarcane decaffeinated coffee contains 20 times less EA than a ripe banana.

body:
Most of you are familiar with the story of Icarus from Greek mythology. Seeking to escape exile from the island of Crete, Icarus and his father, Daedalus, crafted wings out of feathers and wax. Before taking flight, Daedalus urged his son to fly midway between the sun and the sea, warning, “If you fly too low, the sea’s mist will dampen the feathers; if you fly too high, the sun’s heat will melt the wax that binds your wings.” Exhilarated by the power of flight, Icarus ignored his father's warnings and flew too close to the sun, which melted his wings and caused him to fall to his death.
The story of Icarus is thousands of years old, yet its moral remains relevant today: to avoid extremes and seek balance. This wisdom applies to all aspects of life—physical, mental, financial, spiritual, and even in coffee! After countless hours perfecting the blend, roast, and grind, we are proud to introduce our new Greek Coffee Blend: IKARUS.
The blend, roast, and brewing process are inspired by the Greek island of Ikaria, renowned for the longevity of its residents. Along with clean air, olive oil, and a healthy lifestyle, many inhabitants of this BLUE ZONE attribute their long lives to the daily consumption of boiled coffee.
Research shows that boiled Greek Coffee is rich in polyphenols and antioxidants, with a moderate amount of caffeine. Studies link this type of coffee to improved cardiovascular health.
We invite you to bring the taste of IKARUS Greek Coffee into your home!
Net Wt: 12 oz

Kayon Mountain Coffee Farm is located in the Oromia region, in the Odo Shakiso district of the Guji zone. Coffees from the Guji region, such as this one, are well known for their vibrant jam-like fruit characteristics. A 2024 Golden Bean Medalist , this particular coffee has a beautiful, wine-like character in addition to the fruit forward flavors—an incredible combination!
Founded in 2012, Kayon Mountain is owned and operated by Ismael Hassen and his family. Their goal is to produce the high-quality coffee using socially responsible, biodynamic farming practices. Of the 500 hectares his family owns, only half the land is used for farming, with the remainder preserved as wild forest. Coffee plants are grown under a shade canopy of indigenous trees. Compost and natural fertilizers are used to keep plants healthy and organic practices are followed to manage weeds and pests—avoiding the use of harsh chemicals.
Coffee is hand-picked with strict ripeness guidelines. Natural coffees, such as this lot, begin drying the day of picking on raised beds. While drying, the coffee cherries are regularly rotated to ensure even drying. Kayon Mountain owns their own eco-milling equipment, and fully processes their coffee right at the farm.

The King Of Guji Series is a rotating, seasonal offering of beautiful Ethiopian natural processed coffees from the Guji region.
This Qabballe Natural is produced by farmers around Teraga, Oromia, Ethiopia, and processed at the Raro Nensebo Drying Station in Uraga, Guji, operated by Sookoo Coffee and its founder, Ture Waji —widely known as “ The King of Guji. ”
Fifteen contributing producers cultivate farms at an average elevation of 2,225 meters above sea level. The coffee primarily consists of local varieties 74110 and 74112.
At the station, an extensive sorting process removes over and under ripe cherries. The coffee is then dried on African beds under the full sun, following Sookoo Coffee’s strict drying protocols. This process reduces the risk of over-fermentation and defects. The standard drying time for their coffee is between 21-28 days, ensuring optimal flavor development.
Qabballe Natural is able to score an exceptional 86+ on the global quality scale.
It features intense fruity/floral notes like blueberry, raspberry, peach, and jasmine.

MEDIUM ROAST | SOUTH AMERICAN BLEND | ROASTED DAILY IN LA
Escape Blend is our tribute to the rich coffee-growing traditions of South America. This blend combines beans from three of the continent's finest origins — Brazil, Peru, and Colombia — into a smooth, approachable cup with real depth.
TASTING NOTES
A beautiful chocolate-forward profile with layers of cane sugar sweetness and a cherry finish. The Brazilian component provides a full, round body. Peruvian beans contribute a clean sweetness, while Colombian coffee adds cherry-like brightness and complexity.
BEST BREWING METHODS
Escape Blend is incredibly versatile. It shines as a drip coffee or pour over where its chocolate and sugar notes come through clearly. It also makes an excellent Americano or French press. If you enjoy your coffee black, this is the blend to try — its natural sweetness means you won't need to add sugar.
ROASTING APPROACH
We roast this blend to a careful medium level that brings out the natural sweetness of each origin without introducing any bitterness. The result is a clean, smooth cup that tastes just as good at room temperature as it does piping hot.

body:
Gesha is the most name-dropped variety in coffee, which is exactly why we're slow with it. Most of what crosses our cupping table is expensive and forgettable. Then this one: jasmine, bergamot, Earl Grey, lime. All four, every cup, every time we went back to the table. The argument ended there.
Jorge Rojas farms La Roca in Planadas, Tolima, at 1,900 meters. Volcanic ash under everything, up to 2,200 millimeters of rain a year, and cool nights that slow the cherry down and let it build sugar. He and his pickers take ripe cherry only. Whatever doesn't belong gets hand-sorted and floated out before it leaves the farm.
Then the fermentation. Forty-five hours, aerobic, on Cofinet's protocol — long enough to pull the aromatics forward, controlled tightly enough that the fruit never tips over. Then pulped, washed clean, and ten days on parabolic dryers, spread thin and turned by hand.
Gesha punishes heat. The bean is long and thin-walled, and it takes a burner faster than it looks like it should. Push it and the jasmine is the first thing to go, and it does not come back. We sample roasted this lot before we touched the production roaster and watched it hold its moisture all the way through, then release it in one hard spike right at first crack — which told us exactly where the floor was. So we go light. Genuinely light. We drop it seconds after the first crack clears.
In the cup: jasmine first. Then bergamot. Then lime underneath, holding the whole thing up. The body is tea — silky and weightless, but not thin — and if you drink Earl Grey you'll know exactly what's happening here. The finish is long, clean and still floral on the way out.
Give it at least a week off roast if you can. A very light washed Gesha opens slowly, and this one is worth waiting for.
Under 50 bags (12 oz / 340g each). It will not be restocked.
title: La Roca — Gesha Washed

body:
For years everyone assumed Chiroso was a Caturra mutation. It looks like one — short trees, pale green leaves, and it grows the way Caturra grows. Then the genetics came back Ethiopian. That is the whole coffee in one sentence: it looks Colombian and it drinks like something that wandered in from somewhere else. We cupped this lot and wrote the same word down four times. Juicy . So we bought it.
Alex Metrio farms El Silencio in Urrao, Antioquia, between 1,800 and 1,900 meters. Volcanic ash, cold nights, a lot of rain. Chiroso is a high-altitude specialist — it wants the cool, and Urrao gives it plenty, which is why the variety keeps taking top spots at Cup of Excellence out of exactly this corner of Colombia. Ripe cherry only. Everything else is hand-sorted and floated out at the farm.
Then thirty hours underwater. The cherries ferment submerged and sealed before anything gets pulped, calibrated on Cofinet's protocol to build sweetness and acidity together. Then pulped, the mucilage washed off completely, and ten days on parabolic dryers in thin layers, turned by hand.
We roast it light, far enough that some caramel is built and the lime reads as juice instead of raw acid. Not so far that we bury either one.
In the cup: lime up front, bright and round rather than sharp. Caramel underneath, holding it together. Silky body, sweet the whole way through. Optimal for filter — pour over or drip. It pulls a vivid, fruit-forward espresso too if that's how you drink.
Under 50 bags (12 oz / 340g each). It will not be restocked.

Bright, sweet, and built for espresso. Fight the Power brings together fully washed coffees from Kenya and Colombia for a cup that balances vibrant fruit with deep sweetness. Expect notes of passionfruit up front, rounded brown sugar sweetness, and a smooth toffee finish.
THE COFFEE
Fight the Power combines coffees from two celebrated growing origins, bringing together the lively character of Kenyan coffee with the sweetness and structure of Colombian coffee.
The Kenyan component comes from Western and Central Kenya, where ripe coffee cherries are selectively handpicked and carefully sorted before being pulped, fermented, washed, and dried on raised beds. During drying, the parchment is regularly turned and inspected to encourage even drying and maintain quality.
The Colombian component is sourced from cooperatives, associations, and direct partners across Huila, Tolima, Caldas, Risaralda, and Antioquia. Coffee is selectively handpicked, pulped, fermented for 26 to 36 hours, washed, and sun-dried on parabolic beds for up to 20 days.
Together, the two origins create an espresso that is fruit-forward, balanced, and naturally sweet.

body:
Primer Paso
Pre-order only. We roast Primer Paso in 12-pound batches, and a batch is fired when enough pre-orders come in to fill it. Place your order to claim your spot in the next batch — we'll roast it fresh in Stuart and ship it to you. The entire first harvest was just 48 kilograms, and we're already halfway through it. Once it's gone, it's gone forever.
This is the closest we've ever been to the origin of the coffee we roast. Primer Paso is grown exclusively by The Roasted Record on a plot of Finca La Ilusión in Santa Bárbara, Antioquia, in partnership with producer Andrés Cardona, the mind behind Luna Azul.
In 2025 we helped Andrés secure the equipment he needed to process his own cherries. In return, he dedicated a plot of his farm to us for five years. We named it Primer Paso. First steps. The young trees gave their very first harvest in November 2025 — and after the long road of processing, drying, export, and the journey out of Colombia, 48 kilograms of finished coffee finally landed in Stuart in April 2026. Tiny by most measures, but for us, giant.
The trees are young, so this coffee is still finding itself. There's plenty of acidity and real sweetness behind it, though the sweetness is still a little unrefined at this point. We're okay with that.
Each batch's roast is a little different as we refine the profile, so you can taste Primer Paso along with us as we figure out the final steps of a truly farm-to-cup experience.
Primer Paso Natural Anaerobic Process Coffee Tasting Notes: Week 3
Details & Notes
Flavors: Honey, Grapefruit, Red Apple
Body: Medium
Acidity: Bright
Process: Natural Anaerobic
Varietal: Castillo
Elevation: 1,522 MASL
Farm: Finca La Ilusión, Santa Bárbara, Antioquia
Producer: Andrés Cardona, grown exclusively for The Roasted Record
Flavor Profile & Tasting Notes
Week 3 finds Primer Paso settling into something more balanced. The grapefruit and citrus brightness from last week is still here, but a slight adjustment to the drop temperature has brought the honey and red apple back to the forefront. The result is a cup that bridges the first two weeks... fruity sweetness with a abalnced acidity.
The Producer: Andrés Cardona
Andrés Cardona is the producer behind Luna Azul and a partner we've come to trust deeply. When he set out to process his own cherries, we backed him with the equipment he needed, and he set aside a plot of Finca La Ilusión for us in return.
That plot is Primer Paso. Andrés tends the trees on the ground in Santa Bárbara; we shape what happens after the harvest lands in Stuart. It's a true partnership, and it's the closest we've ever been to the coffee we roast.
Read the whole story — the trade, the agronomy program, and every farm report and cupping score sheet — on our Farm Project page, and see how we source everything else on our Coffee Sourcing Philosophy page.

Colombia Supremo Huila is grown certified farms by multiple smallholder farmers in the surroundings area of the town of San Agustín, Huila department. Colombia is the largest producer of washed Arabica coffee and third total highest in the world, after Brazil and Vietnam. Its annual production ranges from 12 million to 15 million 70-kilo (154 lbs) bags. Colombia is very unique and is able to produce coffee all 12 months of the year due to it’s range of micro-climates and terrain. In addition, the primary varieties grown in Colombia are Caturra, Bourbon, Typica and Variedad (resistant to leaf rust disease know as Roya). body:
SUPER OMNIA is our foundation for filter coffee. It is built to perform consistently across batch brew, cold brew, and home brewing setups while maintaining balance and versatility. We specifically created SUPER OMNIA to be approachable and familiar while still maintaining the integrity of specialty coffee. Today, SUPER OMNIA is the base for our batch coffee and cold brew at our cafes and has grown a cult following for our daily customers. SUPER OMNIA shines in the way that it's able to shape to its surroundings, offering a comforting option for practically any brew method.
THE COMPONENTS
SUPER OMNIA is built from two origins that work together to create a stable and versatile profile.
BRAZIL — CERRADO MINEIRO (50%)(https://www.fluidcoffeelove.com/product-page/brazil-cerrado)
This natural process coffee forms the base of the blend. The cherries are dried whole, allowing sugars to fully develop and carry into each batch. This component brings sweetness, body, and a syrupy structure that creates the unmistakable foundation.
HONDURAS — COMAYAGUA, GUAMA DANTA (50%)(https://www.fluidcoffeelove.com/product-page/honduras-guama-danta-comayagua-single-origin-coffee)
This washed coffee provides balance and clarity with careful harvesting and clean processing. Together, they produce a cup that adds structure and definition, preventing the blend from becoming too heavy in body. This half component provides a clear nuance to SUPER OMNIA and further accentuates the "specialty" profile enthusiasts expect from our offerings.
PROCESS
SUPER OMNIA combines natural and washed processing to maintain both sweetness and clarity.
The Brazil component builds depth and body through natural processing.
The Honduras component introduces structure and a clean finish through washed processing.
This balance allows the coffee to remain consistent and adaptable across brewing styles.
COFFEE PROFILE
Brown sugar and milk chocolate lead the cup, creating a smooth and familiar sweetness.
Soft fruit notes move through the middle, adding light complexity without disrupting the structure of the coffee. The finish is clean and balanced, with a rounded body that makes the coffee easy to return to throughout the day.
BREWING THIS COFFEE
SUPER OMNIA is built for filter brewing, with a focus on consistency and ease of use.
BATCH FILTER (HOME DRIP)
Coffee: 60g per liter of water
Ratio: ~1:16
Grind: Medium
This matches how we brew coffee in our cafes and produces a balanced, clean cup.
COLD BREW (IMMERSION)
Coffee: 100g
Water: 800g
Ratio: ~1:8
Grind: Coarse
Steep for 24 hours in a refrigerated or cool environment.
This method produces a concentrated cold brew with high sweetness and body, designed to pair well with milk. Dilute if desired.
POUR OVER (V60 STYLE)
Coffee: 23–25g
Water: 360g

The Founding Roast: Julio Madrid
This coffee marks a rare collaboration with Julio César Madrid Tisnés in Risaralda, Colombia. Three years ago, one of our earliest single origin offerings came from La Riviera Estate--a washed Colombian coffee that left a lasting impression on us with its plum, raisin, mild citrus, and smooth structure.
For our third anniversary, Julio created a custom blend exclusively for Lore, designed as a tribute to that first release. Rather than simply offering a new lot, this coffee was composed to echo the cup that helped begin our work: balanced, elegant, gentle to roast, and deeply familiar in the best way.
The Project
This is not a standard offering. Julio prepared three boxes of 24 kilograms specifically for us, totaling 72 kilograms. From that, only a small number of finished bags will be possible , making this a limited anniversary release tied directly to Lore’s beginning.
